title: Steps field eagerly clamps an empty input to 1, preventing clear-and-retype (inconsistent with min/max draft handling)
description: Both Steps inputs are controlled (`value={steps}`) and their onChange is `onUpdate("steps", Math.max(1, parseInt(e.target.value) || 1))`. When the user clears the field to type a new value, `e.target.value` is "", so `parseInt("")` is NaN, `NaN || 1` is 1, and onUpdate immediately commits `steps = 1`. Because the input is controlled by that committed value, the field snaps back to "1" the instant it is emptied, so a user cannot delete the existing number and type a fresh one (e.g. clearing "21" to type "5" instantly becomes 1). This is the exact intermediate-edit problem the elaborate min/max draft state machine (activeRangeDraft + pendingConfigEcho) was built to solve, but Steps gets no draft handling at all, making the two number fields behave inconsistently. The backend already tolerates a missing/None `steps` (src/haute/_builders.py:859-861 defaults and clamps), so eager clamp-to-1 on every keystroke is unnecessary on the write path.
evidence: L217-219 (standalone) and L283-285 (range) both: value={steps}; onChange={(e) => onUpdate("steps", Math.max(1, parseInt(e.target.value) || 1))}. steps = configField(config, "steps", "") (L67) is controlled, so committing 1 on empty re-renders the field as "1".
